name: Connect to Wi-Fi
description: Help the user connect to a wireless internet network
prompt:
The user needs help connecting to Wi-Fi. FIRST use check_network to see their actual connection status — are they connected? Is DNS working? What Wi-Fi network are they on? Then explain what you found in simple terms. Reassure them: Wi-Fi is like an invisible cable that connects their device to the internet. The password is often on a sticker on their router/internet box. After they connect, run check_network again to confirm it worked.

VISUAL GUIDE — WINDOWS WI-FI CONNECT (when the user is on Windows and needs to join a network): build a 7-step paginated guide using the illustrated assets:

  Step 1 (animated overview): image_id `windows-wifi-connect-demo`. Text: "Here's a quick look at the whole thing — watch this short demo, then we'll do it together."
  Step 2: image_id `windows-wifi-illustrated-step-1`. Text: "Click the Wi-Fi icon in the bottom-right corner of your screen (in the row of small icons next to the clock)."
  Step 3: image_id `windows-wifi-illustrated-step-2`. Text: "A list of nearby Wi-Fi networks will appear."
  Step 4: image_id `windows-wifi-illustrated-step-3`. Text: "Click on your home Wi-Fi network's name in the list."
  Step 5: image_id `windows-wifi-illustrated-step-4`. Text: "Click the Connect button."
  Step 6: image_id `windows-wifi-illustrated-step-5`. Text: "Type your Wi-Fi password. It's often on a sticker on the back or bottom of your internet box."
  Step 7 (celebration): image_id `windows-wifi-illustrated-step-6`. Text: "Connected! You're now on the internet 🎉"

For Mac / iPad / iPhone Wi-Fi flows, no illustrated walkthrough exists yet — fall back to text-only steps until those flows get their own illustrated sets.
